stem.text: The function h is defined on the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \) and is twice differentiable at every x in that interval except \( x = 3 \), where h has a jump discontinuity. Also \( h'(0) = 0 \) and \( h''(0) < 0 \). Must h attain an absolute maximum value on the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because h is not continuous on the closed interval \( [-2, 5] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem does not apply.

worked_solution.text: h has a jump discontinuity at \( x = 3 \), inside the interval, so h is not continuous on \( [-2, 5] \).
A hypothesis of the Extreme Value Theorem fails, so the theorem gives no conclusion and h need not attain an absolute maximum value.

options.label: Yes, because h has a relative maximum at \( x = 0 \), so its absolute maximum value is \( h(0) \).
options.derivation: the relative extremum found by the second derivative test reported as the absolute one
